clue.text: Actually redeem joky promise, breaking Senate oath

indicators.note: something broken comes apart, so the letters of the following words are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A politician has to make good on a jokey pledge, even if it means breaking an oath sworn to the Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: People say 'I'll eat my hat' as a jokey promise that something won't happen; actually doing it means honouring that boast.

clue.text: Part of Capri lovely in springtime

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: found across the end of Capri and the start of lovely

explanation.surface: The Italian island of Capri is at its loveliest in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a month that falls in springtime, an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: This month falls in the Northern Hemisphere spring, so it stands as an example of springtime.

clue.text: Heavy-handedly control work on newspapers

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
the press means newspapers; 'on' places it after the work

explanation.surface: A regime clamps down on the work of the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to rule harshly and unjustly, keeping people under tyrannical control.

clue.text: Pay attention to, commonly — with this?

definitions.text: Pay attention to, commonly — with this?

indicators.note: in common or Cockney speech the initial H is dropped, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to hear is to pay attention to, as in 'hear me out'

explanation.surface: A question about what organ you use to listen when spoken to casually.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the aitch, as in Cockney speech, turns the verb into 'ear; and the closing question points at the organ itself, which is what you hear with.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the organ of hearing, the thing you listen with when you pay attention.

clue.text: Item baked perhaps an awkward responsibility

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a jacket potato fresh from the oven
second meaning: a tricky issue nobody wants to handle

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom pictures something too scalding to hold, so it gets passed quickly from hand to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal baked spud is scalding; figuratively the phrase means a controversial matter that everyone avoids handling.

clue.text: What's sickening to numbers of Romans

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numerals ten, one and a hundred

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what made the ancient Romans ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poisonous makes you ill, so it is literally sickening.

clue.text: Flower is cut: name?

parts.note: to sever is to cut
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A florist asks what a cut flower is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, something that flows; the Severn is Britain's longest river, through Wales and western England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, so setters call one a 'flower'; this is a well-known British river.

clue.text: Conventional pair embracing guy

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
a guy is a rope steadying a tent

explanation.surface: A traditional couple hugging a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the rope holding up a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper behaviour follows the accepted norms, so it is correct and conventional.

clue.text: Prepares to take off one among deductions from pay

indicators.note: a thing placed among others sits in their midst, inside them

parts.note: taxes are taken out of wages
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone notices a single item among the deductions on their payslip.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft taxies along the runway in readiness for its departure into the air.

clue.text: Escape illness with drug

parts.note: flu is a common illness
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Getting off work with an illness and some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escape' reads as a verb, but here it is a noun: an outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney duct is the outlet through which smoke and gases leave a fire.

clue.text: One ironing negligently? It's a hot day!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who burns the clothes they press
second meaning: informal word for a very hot day

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: someone careless with an iron leaves burn marks, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to burn the surface, so a careless presser does it; informally the word also means a blazing summer day.

clue.text: Select cap to be prepared for public display

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked on and made ready, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Choosing a hat to get ready for an appearance in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking show or sight put on for an audience.

clue.text: Modest, but sounding much in demand?

indicators.note: points to how a word is said rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: someone much in demand is chased after

explanation.surface: A demure person who is nonetheless pursued by many admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and virtuous, especially in sexual conduct, so restrained and modest.

clue.text: Deceived and given the chop after half an hour

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: the word taken as written
to be axed is to be given the chop

explanation.surface: Someone was tricked and then sacked within thirty minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the dismissal second, behind the front half of the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a trick, so to be hoaxed is to be fooled or deceived.

clue.text: Staggering, installing new sunshade

indicators.note: to install something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: staggering in the sense of filling with awe
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone tottering about while putting up a new sun canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' looks like lurching about; it means astounding, so awing.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas canopy over a shop window or door that keeps off the sun.

clue.text: Old prison — needs this after violent breakout?

parts.note: surface reading: after a jailbreak smashes the entrance, a replacement is required
setter's reading: the name of a former London jail, which splits into a fresh entrance

explanation.surface: After a violent escape, a historic prison needs repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904; split in two its name describes exactly what a smashed-out jail would need.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was London's main criminal prison for centuries, now gone, so it is an old prison.

clue.text: Almost drop argument for register of singers

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to fall is to drop
a set-to is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Nearly dropping a dispute over the list of choir members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Register' looks like a roll of names, but it is a vocal range.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the high voice above a man's natural range, one of the vocal registers singers use.

clue.text: Fasten up sections that have turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: parts are sections

explanation.surface: Instructions to secure some components that have arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap something is to secure it with a belt or band, fastening it in place.

clue.text: Partners at table accepting one's sensible

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the pair holds the next piece inside them

parts.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table
one is I, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Bridge partners agreeing that someone is level-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, and West partners East.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise means showing good judgement, as does being sensible.

clue.text: Dreadful cost I accepted uncomplaining

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone accepted a terrible price without a murmur.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without grumbling, after the Greek school that taught calm endurance.

clue.text: Satisfied, endlessly wealthy in such a system

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing the system

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: needs that are met are satisfied
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: Someone content and nearly rich within a particular system.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'such a system': the answer names a kind of system, as in the metric system of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal measuring scheme of metres and kilograms is known as the metric system.

clue.text: Keep drawing attention to large jug

parts.note: to flag something is to draw attention to it
keep as in carry on, keep on; it follows the other piece as in 'flag on'

explanation.surface: Someone persists in pointing out a big jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel for serving wine or ale, effectively a big jug.

clue.text: Service charge offered regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A service charge that is applied routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a payment made for professional work, a charge for a service.

clue.text: Choice testimonial on page

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
a reference is a testimonial from an employer

explanation.surface: A selected letter of recommendation printed on a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On page' places the testimonial after the page abbreviation, as in an across entry one piece follows the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference is the option you favour, so it is your choice.
